core.title: Feature URNs follow the profile-declared shape with a {verb}-{object} feature segment, built via the designated URN builder
core.given: A feature URN is being constructed, declared, renamed or referenced in any artifact or code
core.when: The feature URN value is written or changed
core.then: The feature URN must be built through the stack's designated URN-builder construct (profile key urn.builder#artifact) and match the feature-URN shape declared by the profile (profile key urn.feature), both identifier segments lowercase kebab-case, with the feature segment in {verb}-{object} form.
prefer: Use the parent wagon's slug verbatim as the wagon segment.
Shape the feature segment as {verb}-{object}: the verb first, then the object it acts on.
avoid: Hand-assembling feature URN strings instead of using the designated URN builder.
Uppercase, underscores, camelCase, or segments starting with a digit or hyphen.
Noun-only or object-verb feature names (the object placed before its verb).
Omitting the wagon segment or adding extra colon-separated segments.
core.why: The feature URN is the feature identifier, so it must have one fixed, checkable form.
evidence: Every feature URN in the diff matches the feature-URN shape declared by the profile.
Feature URNs are produced through the designated URN builder.
The wagon segment equals the owning wagon's slug.
The feature segment reads as {verb}-{object} (reviewer/LLM judgment).
verification: Shape conformance is mechanical: every feature URN appearing in the change is checked against the profile-declared feature-URN shape.
The {verb}-{object} reading of the feature segment is not mechanically decidable: it is reviewer/LLM-judged, with the first token of the segment expected to be a verb.

The check covers feature URN values and feature-URN construction sites in any artifact or code; it does not cover wagon URNs or other non-feature URNs (acceptance, component, contract ids), which are governed by their own naming conventions.

Activation on the change fact needs a diff-level observer that extracts feature-URN strings and feature-URN construction sites in any file (needs_new_observer); the file_kind, operation and task_term facts are observable now.

values: a value matching a feature URN added or modified
a feature-URN construction site added or modified

fires: A new feature is declared under a wagon with its URN.
A feature is renamed or moved to another wagon, changing its URN.
A plan, wagon, acceptance or documentation artifact adds or updates a reference to a feature URN.
doesNotFire: Editing a feature's description or acceptances without touching any feature URN.
Naming a wagon URN alone (covered by the wagon URN-naming convention).

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete shape every feature URN must match in this stack, fixing the segment order (wagon, then feature) and the segment spelling (lowercase kebab-case).
The stack's single designated construct for constructing URNs programmatically; the core requires feature URNs to be produced through it rather than as hand-assembled strings.

bunOnly.text: Term feature_urn ('the feature identifier.'): values.pattern = ^feature:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ ; values.naming = '{verb}-{object}'.
bunOnly.reason: Names this rule's verifier term id and its value-slot syntax; term/detector/validator ids of a single rule are realization details. The pattern value is carried by profile key urn.feature and the {verb}-{object} naming by the core then and verification, so only the term-id shell is Bun-only.

bunOnly.text: Valid reference examples: feature:resolve-dilemmas:choose-option, feature:manage-inventory:track-stock, feature:manage-users:authenticate-user.
bunOnly.reason: Rule-specific worked examples stay with the reference realization (vocabulary notProfileKeys: rule-specific examples go to the realization); the core keeps only the general {verb}-{object} shape, and the same examples also remain in prefer[1] of bun.json.

neutralityNotes: No stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path remains in the core. 'Wagon' and 'feature' are treated as method-level artifact concepts, not stack names: they parameterize the closed vocabulary itself (urn.<artifact> with artifact in {wagon, feature}, layout.wagon_dir, layout.feature_dir). The Bun regex is carried entirely by profile key urn.feature, while the kebab-case segment spelling is kept in the core as character-level naming consistent with that pattern. URNBuilder.feature had no fitting existing key, so urn.builder#artifact is proposed and also listed in profileRequirements. The three worked example URNs and the verifier term id feature_urn stay in the Bun realization (bunOnly). bun.json has no exceptions (unless is empty) and declares no per-rule severity or disposition, so verification records only checkability (mechanical vs llm_judged), scope/non-coverage, and the needs_new_observer activation fact.
